Notes.Text:
This update for coredns fixes the following issues:

Changes in coredns:

- Update to 1.15.0:
  * Fixes VUL-0: CVE-2026-78669: excessive CPU consumption in HTTP/2 (boo#1285501)
    and CVE-2026-97032: HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder
    race (boo#1287577) by bumping vendored golang.org/x/net to
    v0.60.0.
  * Drops temporary google.golang.org/grpc pin for CVE-2026-84304 as upstream
    now vendors v1.84.0.
  * plugin/cache: cache SERVFAIL when resolver fails without response
  * plugin/forward: support DNS-over-QUIC upstreams
  * core: add opt-in JSON logging with structured DNS query fields
  * New features: SIIT support, expr-lang templates, PROXY protocol v2 metadata
  * Bumped minimum go build requirement to 1.26.0
  * Skip flaky timing/network-sensitive tests in %check (TestHealthMaxFails,
    TestReconnect, TestRace, TestSecondaryZoneNotify, TestPeriodicWeightUpdate)

Vulnerabilities.Description: A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in the client or server by opening a large number of streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values.

HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.
